speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me your age and if you've had any previous fractures from minor falls or bumps? Also, have you ever noticed any unusual curvature in your spine or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of fractures from minor trauma and the unusual features noted at birth, do you experience any excessive hair growth on your face or body, and do you have a family history of similar physical traits or infertility? Also, are you currently experiencing any headaches or vision changes that might suggest a pituitary issue?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any headaches, vision changes, or seizures? Given your history of fractures and the specific genital findings, I need to check your bone density and hormone levels. REQUEST TEST: DEXA scan, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and LH/FSH.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the initial hormone and bone density tests were normal, I need to investigate genetic causes for your ambiguous genitalia and bone fragility. Do you have any family members with similar physical features, short stature, or a history of osteoporosis at a young age? I will now request genetic testing to look for specific chromosomal anomalies. REQUEST TEST: Karyotype, Vitamin D level, and genetic panel for Turner syndrome and osteogenesis imperfecta.

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal karyotype and initial hormone panels, your combination of ambiguous genitalia, delayed menarche, severe acne, and bone fragility strongly suggests a genetic disorder of steroid synthesis rather than a chromosomal issue. Given your mother's history of virilization during pregnancy, I suspect Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, likely the salt-wasting or simple virilizing form with atypical presentation. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone (repeated with early morning draw), Testosterone, DHEAS, and ACTH stimulation test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 17-hydroxyprogesterone: Significantly elevated (12 ng/mL); Testosterone: Elevated (180 ng/dL); DHEAS: Elevated (650 mcg/dL); ACTH stimulation test: Exaggerated 17-hydroxyprogesterone response confirming 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

speaker: Doctor
text: The results confirming 21-hydroxylase deficiency explain your ambiguous genitalia, delayed menarche, and bone fragility due to long-standing androgen excess and glucocorticoid deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Late-onset or Simple Virilizing 21-hydroxylase deficiency).
